text: The energy flux (energy per unit area per unit time) carried by the electromagnetic field is given by the Poynting vector:
explanation: The Poynting vector S = (1/μ₀) E×B gives the directional energy flux of the field. The expressions ε₀E²/2 and B²/(2μ₀) are scalar energy densities, not fluxes, and ε₀ E×B has the wrong prefactor — the correct coefficient is 1/μ₀.
